=Planning=

CHANGES (list ALL modifications, one or multiple):

Change #1: Model Architecture — Add target-encoded interaction features via out-of-fold target encoding (on training rows only) for high-cardinality categoricals and key interaction pairs
- What: Add OOF (nested, fold-safe) target-encoding for the categorical columns and for a small set of domain-meaningful interaction pairs (e.g., coupon x time, coupon x expiration, occupation x income, age x has_children, coupon x direction_opp). Feed these as extra numeric columns to the existing LGBM + HGB blend.
- Why: Current pipeline only uses integer ordinal codes for categoricals (arbitrary order, no signal about per-category acceptance rate). Trees must reconstruct per-category splits from scratch across 700/500 trees; target encoding gives direct per-category statistics. Interaction pairs capture the dominant signal in coupon datasets (e.g., Bar coupons at 6PM to a young single male accepted vs rejected depends on coupon x time x direction).

Change #2: Training Strategy — Fold-safe OOF generation with smoothing, plus per-feature encoder persistence
- What: Fit target-encoding maps inside each StratifiedKFold split of the training data (train-fold statistics applied to val-fold; full-train statistics applied at final-fit). Use additive smoothing (m-estimate, alpha ~10) toward the global prior. Persist the maps (per column, plus interaction pairs) inside the preprocessor pickle so predict-time applies exactly the same mappings without refitting.
- Why: This is required for leakage safety under the contract while providing the benefit. Smoothing stabilizes rare categories (occupation has 25 levels, some with few rows).

WHY current solution limited:
- Root cause: Ordinal-encoded categoricals alone leave the model to learn per-category acceptance rates and coupon x context interactions via axis-aligned splits iteratively; with only ~8.1k rows and 5 coupon types, the crucial signal (which coupon succeeded in which context) is diluted across many splits.
- Evidence: OOF accuracy of the blend ~0.745 gives no clear winner over simpler baselines; missing_counts show categorical columns with heavy levels (occupation 25, income 9, age 8, education 6), and domain knowledge of coupon datasets indicates strong coupon-type and context interactions. The single OOF blend of two tree models with no target statistics for categoricals is likely under-fitting the categorical structure.

HOW these changes address it:
- Mechanism: Target encoding converts each category into a direct estimate of P(accept | category), giving trees a single, information-dense split candidate; interactions give a direct estimate of P(accept | coupon, time) etc. Fold-safe generation prevents leakage, smoothing handles rare categories. This is additive to existing ordinal codes (trees can still split on raw codes).
- Expected improvement: Typically +0.5% to +1.5% accuracy on coupon-acceptance tabular tasks with strong categorical structure. Should push validation accuracy from ~0.746 toward ~0.75-0.76.
- Synergy: Combined with existing LGBM+HGB multi-seed blend, target encoding raises the accuracy ceiling of both base learners, and the OOF weight/threshold search will re-tune around the improved probabilities.

KEEP UNCHANGED (must explicitly list):
- Random seed: 42 (StratifiedKFold shuffle, and model seeds 42/55/68/81/94 for LGBM and HGB).
- Data split: identical 5-fold StratifiedKFold, same splitter settings.
- Label mapping: same class-sorted mapping.
- Blend + threshold search: same grid and OOF selection procedure.
- Predict-time output format: row_id 0..N-1, prediction in original label space.
- LGBM/HGB hyperparameters: unchanged, so the experiment isolates the effect of target encoding features.
- Schema-driven column discovery, missing-value handling (-1 for missing categories) unchanged.
